zh.q: 地球一天转一圈，这一圈是怎么转的？
zh.concl: 地球绕地轴自西向东自转，周期 1 个太阳日 = 24 时（恒星日 23 时 56 分 4 秒才是真正周期），角速度约 15°/时，自转线速度自赤道向两极递减。
points: 地球绕地轴转，方向自西向东；从北极上空看是逆时针，从南极上空看是顺时针。
转一周是 1 个太阳日 = 24 时；以遥远的恒星为参照是 23 时 56 分 4 秒（恒星日），那才是自转的真正周期。
角速度除南北两极点外各纬相同，约 15°/时；线速度自赤道向两极递减，两极点的角速度和线速度都是 0。

zh.q: 地球绕太阳走一圈，轨道和速度有什么讲究？
zh.concl: 公转方向与自转一致（自西向东），轨道是近似正圆的椭圆、太阳在一个焦点上；1 月初近日点、7 月初远日点，近日点公转速度快，所以北半球夏半年比冬半年长 7 天。
points: 公转方向也是自西向东，与自转一致；一周是 1 年（回归年 365 日 5 时 48 分 46 秒）。
轨道是近似正圆的椭圆，太阳位于椭圆的一个焦点上；1 月初经过近日点（1.471 亿 km）、7 月初经过远日点（1.521 亿 km）。
日地距离只变 3 % 左右，但公转速度随之变化：近日点线速度 30.3 km/s、角速度 61′/日，远日点 29.3 km/s、57′/日；地轴空间指向不变。

zh.q: 同一时刻，为什么一半是白天、一半是黑夜？
zh.concl: 太阳只能照亮地球表面的一半，昼半球和夜半球的分界线（圈）叫晨昏线（圈）；地球自转使昼夜不断交替，周期 1 个太阳日。
points: 同一时刻，太阳只能照亮地球表面的一半：向着太阳的半球是白昼（昼半球），背着太阳的半球是黑夜（夜半球）。
昼半球和夜半球的分界线（圈），叫作晨昏线（圈）。这一圈所在的平面永远正对太阳，所以它不随地球转，是地球在它下面转。
昼夜交替的周期是 1 个太阳日；这样的周期长短适宜，白昼不会过于炎热、黑夜不会过于寒冷。

zh.q: 晨昏线上，哪一半是晨线、哪一半是昏线？
zh.concl: 顺自转方向由夜半球进入昼半球的那半圈是晨线，由昼半球进入夜半球的那半圈是昏线；晨昏线上太阳高度为 0°。
points: 一条晨昏圈上，一半是晨线、一半是昏线，判据是自转方向：顺着自转方向由夜进昼的就是晨线。
由昼进夜的另外一半是昏线；地球转下去，晨线上的地方迎来日出，昏线上的地方迎来日落。
晨昏线上各点的太阳高度都是 0°（太阳刚在地平线上）；太阳直射点上太阳高度是 90°。

zh.q: 东边的城市为什么先看到日出？
zh.concl: 地球自西向东转，东边的地点比西边的先看到日出、时间更早；经度每隔 15° 地方时差 1 小时。
points: 地球自西向东转，同一纬度上东边的地点比西边的地点先看到日出，时间也就有了早迟之分。
经度每隔 15°，地方时相差 1 小时（1° = 4 分钟）；越在东边，时间越早。
地方时只跟经度有关、跟纬度无关：同一条经线上各地的地方时相同。

zh.q: 全世界都用地方时不行，怎么办？跨过 180° 为什么回到昨天？
zh.concl: 全球分 24 个时区、每区跨 15°，区时取中央经线的地方时；以 180° 经线划国际日界线，自东十二区向东进入西十二区时间不变、日期减一天。
points: 地方时太碎没法用：全球分 24 个时区、每区跨 15°，以中央经线的地方时为区时；相邻时区差 1 小时，东边早。
东十二区和西十二区各跨 7.5°、合为一个时区：区时相同，但日期差一天（东十二区比西十二区早一天）。
原则上以 180° 经线为「今天」和「昨天」的分界线：自东十二区向东进入西十二区，时间不变、日期减少一天；反过来日期增加一天。

zh.q: 夏至这天，越往北白天越长，长到哪里为止？
zh.concl: 昼长随纬度与季节变化：夏至北半球昼长夜短、纬度越高昼越长，北极圈以北极昼；赤道与二分日全球昼夜等长 12 时。
points: 晨昏线把所经过的纬线分成昼弧和夜弧：昼弧比夜弧长就昼长夜短，反之则昼短夜长。
夏至太阳直射北回归线：北半球昼最长、夜最短，纬度越高昼越长，北极圈及其以北都是极昼；南半球反之。
冬至反过来：北半球昼最短、夜最长，北极圈以北极夜。把日期拖到春分对比一下：晨昏线就穿过南北两极、全球都是 12 小时。

zh.q: 正午的太阳有多高，能不能到头顶？
zh.concl: 正午太阳高度 H = 90° − |φ − δ|，离直射点越近越大；40°N 夏至 73°26′、冬至 26°34′；北回归线以北全年正午太阳在南方。
points: 太阳高度是太阳光线与地平面的交角：直射点上 90°、晨昏线上 0°；正午太阳高度是日内最大的太阳高度。
H = 90° − |φ − δ|，离直射点纬度越近越大；40°N 夏至 73°26′、冬至 26°34′。
纬度分布：二分日由赤道向南北降低、夏至由北回归线、冬至由南回归线降低；北回归线以北全年正午太阳都在南方。

zh.q: 考核：世界杯在莫斯科开幕，北京时间是几点？
zh.concl: 莫斯科东三区当地 17:30 开幕，北京在东八区，相差 5 个时区，所以北京时间是 22:30。
points: 先看两地相差几个时区：莫斯科东三区、北京东八区，差 5 个时区。
越在东边时间越早，所以北京时间 = 17:30 + 5 时 = 22:30。
北京时间是东八区的区时，也就是东经 120° 的地方时，不是北京（116°E）的地方时。

en.q: Earth turns once a day. How does it turn?
en.concl: Earth rotates west to east about its axis with a period of 1 solar day = 24 h (the sidereal day of 23 h 56 min 4 s is the true period), angular speed about 15°/h, and linear speed decreasing from the equator to the poles.
points: Earth turns about its axis from west to east: counterclockwise seen from above the North Pole, clockwise from above the South Pole.
One turn is 1 solar day = 24 h; relative to distant stars it is 23 h 56 min 4 s (a sidereal day), the true rotation period.
Angular speed is the same at all latitudes except the two poles, about 15°/h; linear speed decreases from the equator to the poles, and both are 0 at the poles.

en.q: What is special about Earth's orbit and speed as it goes around the Sun?
en.concl: Revolution runs the same way as rotation (west to east) on a nearly circular ellipse with the Sun at one focus; perihelion in early January and aphelion in early July, with faster motion at perihelion, so the northern summer half-year is 7 days longer than the winter half.
points: Revolution is also west to east, the same as rotation; one orbit is 1 year (tropical year 365 d 5 h 48 min 46 s).
The orbit is a nearly circular ellipse with the Sun at one focus; perihelion is in early January (147.1 million km) and aphelion in early July (152.1 million km).
The Earth–Sun distance changes only about 3 %, but orbital speed changes with it: at perihelion 30.3 km/s and 61′/day, at aphelion 29.3 km/s and 57′/day; the axis keeps its direction in space.

en.q: At the same moment, why is half of Earth in day and half in night?
en.concl: The Sun lights only half of Earth's surface, and the boundary (circle) between day and night hemispheres is called the terminator; Earth's rotation makes day and night alternate with a period of 1 solar day.
points: At any moment the Sun lights only half of Earth's surface: the half facing the Sun is in daylight (day hemisphere), the half facing away is in night (night hemisphere).
The boundary (circle) between the day and night hemispheres is called the terminator. Its plane always faces the Sun, so it does not turn with Earth; Earth turns beneath it.
Day and night alternate with a period of 1 solar day; this period is just right, so days are not too hot and nights not too cold.

en.q: On the terminator, which half is the dawn line and which the dusk line?
en.concl: The half that passes from the night hemisphere into the day hemisphere in the direction of rotation is the dawn line, and the half from day into night the dusk line; the sun's altitude on the terminator is 0°.
points: On a terminator circle, half is the dawn line and half the dusk line, judged by the direction of rotation: the part that passes from night into day with rotation is the dawn line.
The other half, from day into night, is the dusk line; as Earth turns, places on the dawn line see sunrise and places on the dusk line see sunset.
The sun's altitude is 0° everywhere on the terminator (the Sun just on the horizon); at the subsolar point it is 90°.

en.q: Why do cities to the east see sunrise first?
en.concl: Earth turns west to east, so places to the east see sunrise before places to the west and their time is earlier; every 15° of longitude, local time differs by 1 hour.
points: Earth turns west to east, so on the same latitude places to the east see sunrise before places to the west, and time differs accordingly.
Every 15° of longitude, local time differs by 1 hour (1° = 4 minutes); the further east, the earlier.
Local time depends only on longitude, not latitude: all places on one meridian share the same local time.

en.q: Using local time everywhere won't work. What then? And why does crossing 180° take you back to yesterday?
en.concl: The world is divided into 24 time zones of 15° each, with zone time taken from the central meridian's local time; the International Date Line is drawn along the 180° meridian, and going east from UTC+12 into UTC−12 the time stays the same while the date goes back a day.
points: Local times are too fragmented to use: the world is divided into 24 time zones of 15° each, using the local time of the central meridian as zone time; neighboring zones differ by 1 hour, earlier to the east.
UTC+12 and UTC−12 each span 7.5° and together form one zone: same zone time, but the date differs by one day (UTC+12 is a day ahead of UTC−12).

In principle the 180° meridian divides "today" from "yesterday": going east from UTC+12 into UTC−12, the time stays the same and the date goes back one day; the other way, the date goes forward one day.

en.q: On the June solstice, the further north the longer the day. Where does it stop?
en.concl: Day length varies with latitude and season: on the June solstice the Northern Hemisphere has long days and short nights, longer at higher latitudes, with polar day north of the Arctic Circle; at the equator and on the equinoxes, day and night are 12 h each everywhere.
points: The terminator divides each parallel it crosses into a day arc and a night arc: a day arc longer than the night arc means long days and short nights, and vice versa.

On the June solstice the Sun is overhead at the Tropic of Cancer: the Northern Hemisphere has its longest day and shortest night, days get longer with latitude, and everywhere at and north of the Arctic Circle has polar day; the Southern Hemisphere is the reverse.

The December solstice is the reverse: the Northern Hemisphere has its shortest day and longest night, with polar night north of the Arctic Circle. Drag the date to an equinox to compare: the terminator passes through both poles and it is 12 hours everywhere.

en.q: How high is the noon sun? Can it be directly overhead?
en.concl: Noon sun altitude H = 90° − |φ − δ|, larger closer to the subsolar point; at 40°N 73°26′ on the June solstice and 26°34′ on the December solstice; north of the Tropic of Cancer the noon sun is in the south all year.
points: Sun altitude is the angle between the Sun's rays and the horizontal plane: 90° at the subsolar point, 0° on the terminator; the noon sun altitude is the highest of the day.
H = 90° − |φ − δ|, larger the closer the latitude is to the subsolar point; at 40°N, 73°26′ on the June solstice and 26°34′ on the December solstice.

Latitude pattern: on the equinoxes it decreases north and south from the equator, on the June solstice from the Tropic of Cancer, on the December solstice from the Tropic of Capricorn; north of the Tropic of Cancer the noon sun is in the south all year.

en.q: Check: the World Cup opens in Moscow. What time is it in Beijing?
en.concl: The opening is at 17:30 local time in Moscow (UTC+3), Beijing is in UTC+8, 5 zones apart, so Beijing Time is 22:30.
points: First see how many zones apart the two are: Moscow is UTC+3, Beijing UTC+8, 5 zones apart.
The further east, the earlier the time, so Beijing Time = 17:30 + 5 h = 22:30.
Beijing Time is the zone time of UTC+8, that is, the local time at 120°E, not Beijing's own (116°E) local time.
